funding.title: State investment announced
funding.summary: California allocated $1 million to Solana Center. Senator Catherine Blakespear presented the award at Coastal Roots Farm on October 27, 2026.
funding.appropriation: AB 113, Chapter 248, Statutes of 2026; Section 143, Item 3970-101-0001, Provision 1(b).
funding.purpose: The appropriation supports Solana Center's Waste Diversion and Environmental Innovation Program. The award announcement identifies regional compost hubs, school food waste, textile diversion, and reusable products as planned areas of work.
funding.limits: This is an enacted allocation and an announced award. These sources do not establish the payment schedule, spending to date, or a budget for each activity. No funds are allocated to this website concept in the cited records.

initiatives.title: Regional compost hubs
initiatives.summary: Develop and support compost hubs through the Full Circle Soil Project.

initiatives.title: School food waste
initiatives.summary: Work to reduce waste from school lunches.

initiatives.title: Textiles
initiatives.summary: Help keep textiles out of landfills.

sources.title: AB 113 chaptered text, Section 143 — LegiScan mirror

history.title: Neighbors start Solana Recyclers
history.summary: Local residents start a recycling organization and curbside collection program.

history.title: Education becomes the focus
history.summary: A local hauler acquires the collection program. Community education becomes the focus.

history.title: The first Master Composter course
history.summary: The first course takes place at San Marcos landfill.

history.title: A broader mission, a new name
history.summary: Solana Recyclers becomes Solana Center for Environmental Innovation.

history.title: Food scraps return to the farm
history.summary: Solana Center pilots composting at Coastal Roots Farm with farm and restaurant materials.
history.sourceTitle: Senator Blakespear: Coastal Roots Farm pilot history

history.title: California recognizes the compost model
history.summary: The restaurant-and-farm compost model earns a Governor's Environmental and Economic Leadership Award.

history.title: National recognition for organics diversion
history.summary: The U.S. Composting Council names Solana Center its Organics Diversion Program of the Year.

impact.label: students educated
impact.note: Reported by Solana Center. Period follows the PDF cover; the impact webpage retains an older year label.

impact.label: California cities trained to reduce food waste
impact.note: Reported by Solana Center. This counts cities, not people or completed compliance findings.

impact.label: discounted rain barrels distributed
impact.note: Reported by Solana Center. Distribution is an output, not a measured water-savings total.

impact.label: people trained as Master Composters
impact.note: Reported by Solana Center in its 2025–2026 impact report. This training count does not indicate that the former Food Cycle drop-off program reopened.

influence.title: Support for local composting rules
influence.summary: Solana Center supported the County's 2022 organic-materials ordinance update through pilot projects and public input. Senator Blakespear recognized Jessica Toth's role in the revision in 2024.
influence.sourceTitle: Senator Blakespear: 2024 Woman Who Inspires recognition

additionalSources.title: Solana Center: September 14, 2022 ordinance advocacy account

influence.title: Help cities put policy into practice
influence.summary: A February 2020 Encinitas staff report documents a contract with Solana Center to support the City's Plastics Initiative through outreach, education, and work with affected groups.
influence.sourceTitle: Encinitas City Council, February 26, 2020, Item 10A, pages 3–4

influence.title: Share knowledge across the region
influence.summary: County meeting minutes from August 2024 record Jessica Toth's proposal to share municipal ordinance updates, pilot projects, and grant information through an accessible database.
influence.sourceTitle: County Organics Recycling Working Group, August 1, 2024, page 3
